541301|2026-03.headline: Orient Electric Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR948 crores and EBITDA margin improved to 8.2%, though gross margin fell to 31% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR948 crores, up 10% YoY, with Lighting and Switchgear up 16% and ECD up 7.6%. EBITDA rose 15.8% to INR77 crores (8.2% margin) and PAT rose 28.9% to INR40 crores, despite gross margin compressing to 31% from commodity inflation, labour shortage and West Asia gas disruption. For FY26, revenue grew 7.5% to INR3,326 crores, EBITDA rose 12.4% to INR229 crores (about 6.9% margin), and PBT before exceptional items rose 24.2% to about INR139 crores. Calibrated price increases of about 4% in Q4 and roughly 6% in April were taken, and management said these do not fully offset cost inflation.

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY on distribution expansion and premiumisation; consumer lighting grew double digits. High-value luminaires rose to 68% of mix from 63%; professional luminaires were flat. Wires roughly doubled, and switches and switchgear grew high double digits.

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.6% YoY despite industry softness. Fans grew high single digit; BLDC grew over 50% and is 25% of domestic ceiling fan revenue. Premium mix is about 35% of domestic fan revenue, up from 30% last quarter.

segments.commentary: Appliances (heating, garment care) grew high double digits and e-commerce grew high double digits; quick commerce is 10% of digital channel. Exports grew double digits, with TPW a significant part.

Management remains committed to reaching double-digit EBITDA margins structurally once commodity inflation and supply disruptions subside; no specific timeline was given.
Gross margin guidance of 32-34% is unchanged, with Q4 running about 100-150 bps below it.
No FY27 numerical guidance was given; no share buyback is planned at present.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant utilisation is improving; TPW production is split between Kolkata and Hyderabad, and the plant is a hub for southern and export supply.

New products include Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching fan, about INR16,000), Aerosilent (under 50 dB, about INR8,000) and an inverter battery backup fan (about 6 hours of backup).
demand_pricing: Price increases: about 2.5-3% in January, 1-1.5% in March, and about 6% in April; fans, lighting and switchgear each about 6%, and wires increased roughly every 2-3 weeks.
Management says the incremental cost impact was slightly lower than the industry because part of its portfolio needed little spec change.
Market share gained about 30-40 bps per third-party data, described as broad-based across channels and markets, not limited to BLDC.
Channel inventory was elevated, and dealers were cautious on replenishment; Q4 channel build was described as normal.
Consumer offtake is about 45% in March-June and 55% in the balance of the year; premium and BLDC demand is more linear.
Cost pressure: labour shortage, commercial LPG unavailability, and minimum wage hikes of 35% in Haryana and 24% in UP.

qa_highlights.question: How much more price hike is needed to pass on the full incremental cost, and where are the fan market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price action was staggered (about 4% in Q4, about 6% in April) and the incremental impact was lower than the industry. Market share gains of 30-40 bps were broad-based across channels, not confined to BLDC.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise to over 30 from 23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher inventory built to hedge supply disruptions and higher payables.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the double-digit EBITDA margin target slipped, and when will it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 100-150 bps gross margin hit from the lag in price action in March. It remains committed to double-digit margins once commodity inflation and supply disruptions ease, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin not improved despite a higher premium mix and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases do not fully offset commodity inflation, and labour productivity, LPG costs and wage hikes add further cost pressure. Premiumisation has helped EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2026 a year of protecting margins, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 was a washout and H2 exited with better EBITDA margins. It gave no numerical FY27 guidance and said challenges remain.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing now a structural tailwind toward INR3,000 crore revenue and INR100 crore profit over FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see this as pricing power, calling it a catch-22 industry situation. It pointed to consumer-led product value as the real pricing power and said the aim is INR5,000 crore revenue with double-digit EBITDA.

541301|2026-06.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 saw a strong summer-led demand recovery from mid-April, with revenue up 23.5% YoY and ECD revenue up 22.7% to INR669 crores. Gross margin moderated to 29.8% under commodity and labour cost pressure, but EBITDA margin rose 102 bps YoY to 7% as fixed-cost discipline and Project Sanchay savings (INR10 crores) offset the pressure. Management took multiple calibrated price increases across categories, with fans cited at around 15-16% cumulative since December. Management declined to give margin guidance, reiterating only an aspiration of 32-34% gross margin and continued path to double-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: ECD (Fans, Appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR669 crores, up 22.7% YoY, with high double-digit fan growth and double-digit appliance growth. BLDC grew 36% YoY and new products were 30% of fan revenue; premium mix reached 36% of domestic fan revenue.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Consumer (B2C) lighting grew high double digits; B2B/C-Loom grew high single digits, with tender business deliberately reduced. Lighting margin declined 40 bps YoY due to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity costs. High-value looms share rose to 60%, up 500 bps.

segments.name: Switchgear and Switches
segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Wires
segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew double digits, led by Africa and SAARC; Middle East was impacted. Hyderabad plant certifications completed over the last 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a 32-34% gross margin, but declined to guide given volatile inflation.
Management is committed to a path to double-digit EBITDA margin; timing depends on inflation. EBITDA margin trend: 5.3% (3 years ago), 6.6%, 6.9%, 8.2% in Q4, 7% in Q1 FY27.
Further Sanchay accruals expected in Q2 FY27 after INR10 crores in Q1.
Long-term aim of a healthy double-digit revenue CAGR; first milestone of INR5,000 crores revenue, with a prior 14-15% CAGR framework.
Marketing spend held at 4.4-4.5% of revenue (5.5% last year on the old basis, per management's comparison).
Management expects employee cost to stay range-bound as a percentage of sales, with automation helping over the long term but not in Q2.
capex_capacity: Ongoing automation of plants and processes to reduce labour cost dependence; benefits expected over the long term rather than in Q2.
Hyderabad plant is a core export base; international certifications completed.
Continued capex on new products, maintenance and capacity enhancement, described as spent as required rather than cut.
New product launches: Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching ceiling fan), Aerosilent (under 50 dB), Ecotech Volt; 3 Red Dot Design awards won.
demand_pricing: Demand: cooling net demand revived from mid-April and stayed robust through May, moderating toward quarter end. Management said Q1 was a balanced sell-in and sell-out quarter with no inventory build-up.

Pricing: fans had 6 price increases from December to June, cumulatively about 15-16%, with about 10% sequential QoQ in fans. Appliances had about 4 increases (high single to double digit). Lighting rose about 10% over 5-6 months. Switchgear rose high double digit. Wires are priced with a 15-day lag to LME.
Competition: management said most leading brands did not take a June price increase, while start-up brands took about half of Orient's increase. Orient says it has priced slightly ahead of peers.
DTM network added about 3,600 retailers in the quarter. E-commerce grew double digits.
Management said Chinese TPW fans are more price-competitive than Indian products; Europe entry is targeted before the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ECD growth came from price increases, and how much more pricing is needed to offset raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume plus value across categories, with fans taking about 6 increases from December to June (about 10% sequential in Q1). It said further price action will be calibrated to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is there trade inventory build-up in Q1, and how do DTM and non-DTM markets compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory build-up and the quarter was secondary-led. Both DTM and MD markets grew healthy double digits with volume growth, and no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin recover in Q2 and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 32-34% gross margin aspiration but gave no guidance. It said some commodity prices reversed in recent days, Sanchay accruals will continue, and it will act calibrated to inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY, and was ad spend cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend was flat in value YoY, with a shift from IPL to digital and premium media. Marketing was 4.5% of sales versus 5.5% last year and is planned at 4.4-4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs keep rising, and is operating leverage exhausted?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 10.7% YoY because of minimum wage increases, but fell to 8.9% of sales from 9.9% a year ago. Management expects it to stay range-bound as a share of sales, with automation as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lighting margin decline and B2B performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the 40 bps lighting margin decline to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity increases. B2C grew high double digits, B2B C-Loom grew high single digits, and tender business was cut deliberately.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, LME-linked wires) and pass-through lag, which compressed gross margin to 29.8%.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage increases, with employee cost up 10.7% YoY.
Price-led growth may be tested if the industry does not follow Orient's price increases; start-up brands priced below it.
Quarter-end demand moderation and festive-season sentiment; channel inventory normalisation.

541301|2026-09.headline: Orient Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR27 crores, but gross margin fell to 29% on inflation.
541301|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue at INR1,829 crores (+24.3%). EBITDA rose 49.7% YoY to INR57 crores, with margin up 106 bps to 6.5%, helped by Project Sanchay savings of about INR13 crores in the quarter. Gross margin was 29% in Q2 (29.4% in H1) as copper, aluminium, steel, plastics and crude-linked inputs kept rising faster than price increases. Management said gross margin should recover only as inflation slows, and it held a long-run gross margin guidance of about 32% and a double-digit EBITDA margin aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by input cost pressure; H1 29.4%

financial_highlights.value: About INR13 crores in Q2; about INR23 crores in H1

financial_highlights.change: Up from about 16-17 days in FY24 per analyst

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue INR329 crores, +25.7% YoY. Consumer lighting grew double digits; professional lighting grew high single digits; wires more than doubled YoY; switchgear and switches grew high double digits. High-value looms were 66% of loom mix.

segments.name: Electrical Consumer Durables (ECD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR550 crores, +24.9% YoY. Fans grew high double digits and gained share; BLDC grew about 26% YoY and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix; premium fans about 40% of fan mix. Appliances grew double digits led by water heaters and garment care.

guidance_outlook: Long-run gross margin guidance held at about 32%; management said gross margin recovery depends on inflation slowing.
Double-digit EBITDA margin remains the aspiration; management expects margins to trend closer to it within the next four to six quarters, with H2 better than Q2.
Revenue CAGR guidance raised to more than 15% (previously 15%-plus), with H1 growth at 24.3%.
Working capital expected to fall back to about 20 days over the next four to six quarters via channel financing programs.
Project Sanchay expected to exceed last year's full-year savings of about INR70 crores in H2 FY27 as accruals rise.
Hyderabad plant utilisation expected to rise in Q3-Q4 for next-season production; steady-state margin benefit of about 20-30 bps.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad facility at about 40% capacity utilisation on a single shift; mix about 75% PPW and 20-25% ceiling fans, largely TPW facilities.
Hyderabad to start producing models that sell well in South to cut logistics and warehousing costs.
About 80% of PCBs used in BLDC fans are made in Orient's own lighting factories.
Working capital at 34 days, with cash discipline prioritised alongside portfolio investment and distribution expansion.
demand_pricing: Price increases: fans about 9% in Q1, about 3% in Q2 and about 3% in October; appliances about 6% in Q1 and about 3% in Q2; lighting 6-7% in Q1, about 6% in Q2 and about 2% in October; switchgear 7-8% in Q1 and 6% in Q2; wires raised every 2-3 weeks as a fast follower.
Price increases recovered about 80% of inflation in fans, about 90% in appliances, nearly 100% in wires and 80-100% in other categories, per management.
Management said there was no abnormal primary up-stocking from price hikes; Q2 pull was split between September and October with Diwali timing.
Quick commerce about 15% of digital revenue, growing about 100% YoY; e-commerce grew high double digits.

Added about 3,000-4,000 fan outlets within a base of more than 1 lakh direct and indirect distribution points; DTM expanded to Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and into Punjab and Nagpur service.
BLDC ASP index about 1.11 vs industry average of 1, up from 1.04 over six quarters.
B2B is double digit overall; about 25% of lighting business is B2B; B2B growth has been slower than B2C.
Gross margin decline of about 250 bps over two quarters attributed by management to input inflation rather than under-pricing; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Did price hikes cause inventory up-stocking in September, and is there any one-off in growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes since April have not led to abnormal primary up-stocking; Q2 season buying was split between September and October, with no one-off effect.

qa_highlights.question: How big is BLDC as a share of sales and what are the plans to grow it?
qa_highlights.answer: BLDC grew about 26% YoY, consistently for 8 quarters, and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix versus about 17-18% for the industry excluding large BLDC players.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend and how is new product success measured?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 0.8-0.9% of turnover; NPDs are about 30% of fan revenue with a 90%-plus commercialisation success rate, tracked by reach, repeats and third-party market share.

qa_highlights.question: When can operating margin reach double digits, and why is working capital at 34 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to get much closer to double digits in H2 onwards, within four to six quarters, if inflation eases. Receivable days rose due to DTM and new segments; channel financing should bring working capital back to about 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth and pricing trajectory move FY27 growth towards a 15%-plus CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth was 24.3%; management guided to more than 15% CAGR, which is slightly more aggressive than the earlier guidance, with volume growth expected to rise as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 250 bps over two quarters despite price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflation has outpaced price increases, pricing has been passed on ahead of peers, and BLDC ASP indexing improved to 1.11; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also contributed.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to about 32% depends on inflation easing; copper touches new highs about every two weeks and steel moved from about 65 to above 80.
Competitive intensity and unorganised players taking share at the bottom of the pyramid could limit further price pass-through.
Working capital at 34 days versus target of about 20 days; receivables rising with DTM expansion.
Wires expansion is limited to North, East and parts of South; pan-India launch not yet done.
Project Sanchay savings need to step up in H2 to beat FY26 full-year level of about INR70 crores.
Hyderabad plant utilisation at about 40% on single shift.
541301|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and growth, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly said inflation has outpaced pricing and gave no firm timeline for double-digit EBITDA or 32% gross margin. Responses on working capital and gross margin drew some pushback and were answered with qualified, forward-looking explanations.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, as we speak, there is no predictability on the inflation.
So, there are gaps to be covered yet, and that's a competitive intensity that's there in each of the categories, and that's what we've always looked at it.
Yes, it's a sharp drop of about 250 basis point, but that's not because we've not passed as much as our competitive intensity allows us to pass.

rows.label: Project Sanchay savings above FY26 level
rows.why: Savings were about INR13 crores in Q2 and about INR23 crores in H1, and management expects H2 to exceed last year's full-year savings of about INR70 crores as accruals rise.

rows.why: Utilisation at Hyderabad is about 40% on a single shift and is expected to rise in Q3-Q4 for next-season production, with a steady-state margin benefit of about 20-30 bps.

541302|2026-06.headline: Dhruv Consultancy Q1 FY27 net sales fell to INR15.55 crore with an operating loss of about INR3 crore, while Q1 order inflow reached about INR90-100 crore.
541302|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales were INR15.55 crore and total income INR15.95 crore, with management attributing the operating loss to estimate corrections, tax reversals and a fixed-cost base ahead of revenue conversion. Management said Q1 order inflow was about INR90-100 crore, including a INR40.92 crore OBCC order, the largest ticket the company has booked. Unexecuted order book is stated at INR300 crore, with the company also citing a total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer. Management guided that billing on new orders starts around Q3 and that the company is entering wayside amenities through a 55% SPV. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, citing SEBI LODR constraints.

541336|2026-03.headline: IndoStar Q4 FY26 net loss of INR424 crores on INR326 crores extra SR provision and INR49 crores West Asia overlay, despite 17% QoQ disbursement growth to INR1,306 crores.
541336|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a repair-and-transformation year: tighter underwriting, portfolio diversification away from MHCV, opex cuts under Project Leap, and legacy security receipt (SR) clean-up. Q4 disbursements rose 17% QoQ and 21% YoY to INR1,306 crores, and AUM reached INR8,056 crores, up 5% QoQ. Q4 was loss-making because of an additional INR326 crores provision on SRs, a INR49 crores management overlay for West Asia risk, and about INR55 crores of extra ECL charge from the annual model refresh. Management guided to a 3-year framework through FY29 with 35% disbursement CAGR, PAT of INR450-500 crores, and a loan book of INR16,000-17,000 crores.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements INR1,254 crores (+15% QoQ from INR1,087 crores) at 17.2% yield; AUM over INR7,500 crores. MHCV share of disbursements cut to 31% in FY26 from 57% in FY24, while passenger vehicles rose to 23% from 8%.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements INR52 crores (+73% QoQ from INR30 crores) at 21.8% yield; AUM INR175 crores. Average ticket about INR7.5 lakh, LTV below 40%, tenure about 7 years; 1+ DPD at 0.3%. Live in 108 branches.

segments.name: Security Receipts (legacy)
segments.commentary: Balance sheet SRs of INR1,608 crores from an original pool of INR2,086 crores; about INR470 crores (around 30%) recovered. Additional INR326 crores provision lifts coverage to about 63%, leaving net carrying value about INR589 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY29 targets: 35% CAGR in disbursements, PAT of INR450-500 crores, loan book of INR16,000-17,000 crores; management said the PAT target is for FY29, not FY27.
Normalized credit cost of 2-2.25% once the old book runs off (earlier stated as 2-2.5%); Stage 3 to stabilize at 3.75-4%.
Plans to add about 100 branches over three years; productivity gains of 10-15% per portfolio; opex to rise only marginally in FY27.
April plus expected May FY27 disbursements tracking about 40%+ YoY; Project Leap savings of INR51 crores annualized, INR27 crores realized in FY26.
Micro LAP to launch in at least 2 more states in FY27; target yield about 20% for at least 12-24 months.
SR cash flows expected over roughly 18-36 months; redemptions on large construction projects to start after 12-15 months.
Management overlay of INR49 crores to be held for about 12 months.
capex_capacity: Frontline sales force expanded 30% in H2 FY26 to about 1,600 at 31 March 2026, now about 1,700.
Network of 454 branches across 24 states and UTs (described elsewhere as 23 states); about 5,000 employees.
Micro LAP live in 108 branches of the 454; calibrated rollout planned.
Digital adoption at 84% in vehicle finance and near 100% in Micro LAP; VF lead-to-disbursement TAT cut 25%; eKYC approval received.
Strategic focus limited to vehicle finance and Micro LAP for the next 3 years.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield 17.2% in vehicle finance; management says targeted yield of about 17%+ supports 2-2.25% normalized credit cost.
Customers with CIBIL above 725 rose to 79-80% from 63% in FY24; New-to-Credit exposure fell to 4% from 13%.
New-underwriting book about 60% of portfolio; expected 75% by September 2026 quarter.
Non-starter rate (0+ DPD disbursed in last 6 months) fell to 1.05% from 3.29%.
Micro LAP: management says 20% yield holds for loans up to INR10-12 lakh; loans above INR15 lakh still show about 19% IRR.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further provisioning on the SR book, and when will the construction-project SRs roll off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stressed assets are largely provided for. SR net carrying value of INR589 crores is expected to be realized over about 18-36 months, with redemptions on large construction projects starting after 12-15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the additional INR490 crore buffer (INR326 crores SR plus INR49 crores overlay plus about INR55 crores ECL refresh)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the SR provision as prudence, the INR49 crores overlay as an anticipatory West Asia buffer, and the ECL refresh as revised LGD and PD inputs. It said no stress is visible in the portfolio and that the overlay will be held for about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stage 3 aspiration, and is a 2-2.5% credit cost achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 3 is expected to settle at 3.75-4%, with a gradual decline through the year. Normalized credit cost is targeted at 2-2.25% once the old book runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Are slippages coming mainly from the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed. It said old-cohort delinquency is falling month on month across buckets and that bounce rates are declining.

qa_highlights.question: How is opex expected to behave with disbursements growing 35-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects opex to rise only marginally in FY27, with AUM and revenue growing much faster than costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR450-500 crore PAT target for FY27 or FY29, and does it assume a 2% credit cost and 9% funding cost?
qa_highlights.answer: It is for FY29. Management said it reflects the current 9% incremental borrowing cost and the 2-2.25% normalized credit cost, and that these are not base or worst case. Rating upgrade could lower funding costs further.

risks_watch: Credit quality: gross Stage 3 rose to 4.8% and Q4 slippages were high; the old book is still a large share until about September 2026.
Fuel price increases and West Asia crisis could hit SRTO and fleet customers; management has a INR49 crores overlay and says it would tighten policy if stress appears.
SR recovery timing (18-36 months) and the INR589 crores net carrying value depend on construction-project progress.
Growth ramp versus 35% CAGR target and 100-branch expansion; execution and cost discipline must hold while opex is kept flat.
Management declined to give Q4/Q3 interest reversal and NPA amounts on the call, so interest income flatness is not yet explained.
541336|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, funding cost and portfolio trends, with explicit forward targets. More cautious on the macro: it says no stress is visible but has built a buffer. Evasive on the interest-reversal question, which it deferred to a follow-up.
key_quotes: We do expect that this provision will remove the SRs from the list of considerations investors have as they evaluate IndoStar.
And as old book runs out, you would start seeing us stabilizing around 2% to 2.5% credit cost, which is what we're targeting as our yield is about 17% plus.
And if that were to happen, we will tighten our policies and choose portfolio quality over growth in the short term.

541336|2026-06.headline: IndoStar Q1 FY27: disbursements up 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore and PAT of INR11 crore, versus a loss of INR424 crore in Q4 FY26.
541336|2026-06.overview: Disbursements rose 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore, though slightly lower QoQ, with disbursement yield at 17.6%. PPOP was flat at INR92.9 crore and credit cost fell sharply to INR81.4 crore from INR517.3 crore in Q4, which drove PAT of INR11 crore. Collection efficiency dipped to around 95% and the company held a INR529 crore average excess liquidity buffer that added about INR8 crore of negative carry.

541336|2026-09.headline: IndoStar Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR13 crore on a INR49 crore overlay release; disbursements up 51% YoY to INR1,399 crore.

Net total income was INR242 crore versus INR190 crore a year earlier, and PAT was INR13 crore versus INR11 crore. Reported profit was helped by the release of a INR49 crore precautionary overlay created in Q4 FY26, while the credit cost was INR96 crore. Gross Stage 3 fell to 4.5% from 4.8%, and management said legacy pre-January 2025 book is running down toward about 10% of AUM by end-FY27.

541403|2026-03.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but gross margin fell 169 bps to 28.1% on mix and cotton costs; price hikes of 4-6% planned.
541403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore and volume grew 12.0%, but gross margin compressed 169 bps to 28.1% as the economy segment rose to 47% of revenue and cotton/yarn costs rose. Operating EBITDA grew only 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin), while PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income rose 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, EBITDA 9.3% to INR200 crore (10.6% margin) and PAT 18.0% to INR107 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in April (3-4%) and plans another 2-3% in June, and it deferred FY27 guidance to the Q1 call.

qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.

Management chose not to match market discounting, so revenue growth was limited and volume declined 1.6% YoY, mainly from Dollar Man. PAT rose 22.1% to INR 26 crore and net debt fell to INR 192 crore from INR 277 crore at March 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 11-13% and operating EBITDA margin of 11.5-12.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry price hike sustainable, and will the volume decline be recovered in the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects pricing and discounting to stabilise over one to two quarters. It targets double-digit volume-plus-value growth for FY27, with full-year revenue growth of about 11-12% internally and 11-13% guided.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and can it be sustained without further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Two drivers: the 4-5% price hike and not matching competitor discounts, which held revenue growth to about 1.5%. Management said low-cost inventory was a small contributor, as input prices rose from late February and the hike came in April. It sees no further hike needed as yarn and cotton have stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drove the volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dollar Man volume fell about 3-3.5%, the main driver of the total 1.6% volume decline. Socks fell about 7% but are only about 2% of sales. Dollar Woman grew 1.5-2% in volume and Dollar Always was flat YoY.

Ad spend breakdown: about INR 100-102 crore a year across digital, TV, IPL, hoardings and in-store branding.

INR 86 crore of debt was repaid in Q1, and total debt (about 90% working capital) is targeted at zero by FY28. Q1 operating cash flow was about INR 96 crore.

The Board has appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen, with a conclusion expected in H1 FY27, and the polymers carve-out from CRAMS is on hold. Debt was cut by about INR 158 crores in FY26 to a line of sight of about INR 503 crores by end-May 2026, and management has an internal target of being debt-free by FY29. No FY27/FY28 numerical outlook was given.

541729|2026-03.headline: HDFC AMC FY26 profit after tax rose 16% to INR28.6 billion; QAAUM grew 20% to INR9.3 trillion and dividend of INR54 per share was recommended.
541729|2026-03.overview: HDFC AMC closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR41.2 billion (up 18% YoY), operating profit of INR32.1 billion (up 18%, 35 bps of AUM) and PAT of INR28.6 billion (up 16%). QAAUM reached INR9.3 trillion (up 20%), with equity-oriented AUM at INR6 trillion and unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million. Management highlighted record March 2026 SIP flows of INR321 billion industry-wide and said investor behaviour during the market correction was disciplined. The major open issue is the SEBI base expense ratio (BER) change effective April 1, 2026, which management expects to offset through commission changes with no material P&L impact.

segments.name: Equity-oriented funds
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion. Actively managed equity yield was about 60-61 bps, versus 56 bps including index funds.

segments.name: Debt and liquid funds
segments.commentary: Debt yield was 28 bps and liquid 13 bps in Q4. Management said the balance sheet debt book is run with modest duration and largely passive management.

segments.name: Alternatives, PMS and international
segments.commentary: Alternatives margins are marginally above equity margins, and discretionary PMS is in line with equity margins. Non-discretionary EPFO/SPFO mandates earn thinner net economics. GIFT City has five live funds, all wholly owned.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gross impact of the base expense ratio change on existing book at about 3-4 bps, to be largely offset by commission restructuring and cost management, so targeted P&L impact is not material.
The 5 bps trail previously paid in lieu of exit load has been removed, and GST on management fees now sits outside the expense ratio, requiring margin adjustments.

No formal cost guidance is given. Employee cost ex-ESOP grew about 12.5% YoY, with five-year CAGRs of about 13% for employee cost and 13.5% for non-employee cost; costs are expected to grow broadly in line with business.
Management said flow market share is above book market share, and the company will launch SIF products only after careful design, not as a race.
Management said the SEBI-classified category presence is complete and new launches will be selective, with focus on sharpening existing funds.
capex_capacity: Physical branch network significantly expanded over the last couple of years, with further expansion under evaluation.
Investment in AI, cloud technology, cybersecurity and talent for PMS, international and alternatives; management called these foundational investments.
Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.
Seven new schemes launched in FY26, and first close of a private credit fund with IFC as partner and anchor investor announced.
Two EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates won. SPFO is already being managed, and the EPFO agreement is being signed.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 net inflows INR7.4 trillion, with equity-oriented funds about INR4.9 trillion; March 2026 SIP collections INR321 billion (up 24% YoY, 97 million contributing accounts). Industry market share is around 12.8-13% for the last eight to nine quarters.
HDFC AMC: direct plans about 31% of equity AUM; 97% of transactions digital; total accounts above 30 million; unique investors 16.7 million, up 3.5 million, versus industry addition of 7.2 million.
Unique investor penetration rose from 17.6% (March 2023) to 27% (March 2026). Folios rose from 2.3 crore to 3 crore, and SIP and STP flows were INR48.8 billion in March 2026 (up 33% YoY).

Management said flow share is higher than book share across channels, including fintech and HDFC Securities. HDFC Bank share of the distribution pie is declining, which management attributed to broad-based growth across other channels.
Competitive pressure: management stated SBI is almost closed-architecture, and some banks are more guided in retail distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new TER/BER regulation and how will distribution commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross impact on the existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset through commission optimisation and cost management, so no material P&L impact is targeted. New commission structures already reflect removal of the 5 bps exit-load trail, and the company will share more detail over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a third-party calculation show Q4 flow market share below Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the calculation missed IDCW (dividend) payouts in Q4 that were recorded as redemptions; the company does not accept the computed figure. Management said overall flow share remains above book share.

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds remain in the top two quartiles across most categories and that many are rated 4 or 5 stars by Value Research. It pointed to long-term alpha track records, with 12-13 funds having 15-year-plus records.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

risks_watch: SEBI base expense ratio change from April 1, 2026: margin effect depends on commission restructuring, and management said the impact is not yet quantified precisely.
Sustainability of flows if markets stay weak for longer; management cautioned that investor behaviour has not been tested over an extended downturn.
HDFC Bank channel share is declining, and management said the bank remains open architecture, with event-driven flow variability.
Rising costs from talent, technology and AI investments versus margin targets, with no formal cost guidance.
Alternatives and PMS economics are thinner for non-discretionary government mandates (EPFO/SPFO), and SIF launch timing is undefined.
Mark-to-market exposure on the SEBI skin-in-the-game equity holdings on the balance sheet.

541929|2026-06.headline: Synergy Green Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹75.71 crore and 7% PBDIT margin were weak; management reiterates ₹500 crore FY27 revenue and 300 bps margin uplift.
541929|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was ₹75.71 crore with absolute PBDIT of ₹5.3 crore at a 7% margin, as dispatches slipped on customer lifting, prototype approval delays and shipping constraints. Production rose about 10% YoY and the new 45,000 tpa capacity reached 66% utilisation in Q1, with July utilisation at 85% (about 3,200 tons). Raw material, consumable and energy inflation (linked to the West Asia conflict and an MSEDCL solar banking change) cut margins, which management expects to partly recover from Q2 via one-quarter-lagged indexation. Management maintained FY27 guidance of ~₹500 crore revenue (33% growth) and ~300 bps PBDIT margin expansion.

segments.name: Wind foundry (SG iron, grey iron, steel castings, 3-30 MT)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 tpa; FY26 utilisation was 93% on old capacity. Q1 utilisation 66% on new capacity, July at 85%, with 80-90% targeted within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Machining (in-house)
segments.commentary: Machining capacity 20,000 tpa; product development 50% complete and utilisation reached 50% in July. Target 40-50% in-house machining, reducing outsourcing costs.

segments.name: Non-wind (power, mining, L&T, BHEL, Terex)
segments.commentary: BHEL PO received in Q1 (8-9 months development); L&T development underway. Terex order book strong on yen appreciation (~20% vs INR). Non-wind and gearboxes ~30% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance ~₹500 crore (33% growth), reiterated despite weak Q1.
FY27 full-year PBDIT margin to improve ~300 bps YoY, driven by volumes, export concentration in H2 and machining contribution.
Q2 expected to see indexation recoveries on raw material (~200 bps) and partial consumables recovery; new customer revenues from Q2.
Utilisation target of 80% on full 45,000 tpa capacity for FY27; 80-90% within 2-3 months from July.
Executable order book positioned at ₹500 crore for FY27; ₹600 crore achievable next year with higher capacity.
Land for 100,000 tpa project targeted by December or March; next project start by Q3 of next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa (expanded from 30,000 tpa); in-house machining 20,000 tpa; 10 MW captive solar.
Plan for 100,000 tpa capacity; land acquisition targeted by December or March; greenfield capex takes 15-18 months to commission.
Additional 5 MW wind PPA via open access to offset power cost inflation; solar + PPA to cover 50-60% of power needs.
Vestas 4 MW platform: tooling started mid-May; samples expected Q4 FY27, full production Q1 FY28. Nordex NX N 5 MW prototypes cleared in Q1.
Inventory held at 8-10 weeks; target to keep shop order book below 8 weeks.
demand_pricing: Q1 dispatches lower due to delayed customer material lifting and prototype approvals with a key customer; export rollouts hit by ship availability amid West Asia conflict. Unsold production went into inventory.
Furan Resin (third-largest cost item) rose ~60%; PNG/LNG prices up 60-70%; pig iron and CRC inflation from shortages and imported scrap logistics.
Realisations expected to rise from ₹138-140/kg to ₹145+ levels in coming quarters; management said no change in realisation in Q1.
Vestas ~40-45% of business historically, expected to fall toward ~30% as new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) are added; Nordex growing; Adani 3.3 MW in serial production.
Indian suppliers estimated 5-10% cheaper than China on landed cost for wind products after yen appreciation; US market favours non-Chinese suppliers.
Management views wind demand stronger than solar; night-time wind tariffs 25% higher than solar daytime, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Could the ₹500 crore FY27 target slip into next year given slow offtake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 production was strong but did not convert to sales; Q2 execution is at a much higher flow rate, and product approval has come from 50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: Did realisations spike given 66% utilisation implies ~7,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said produced material was not all sold, creating inventory, and realisation is unchanged, with revenue recognition pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income of ₹4.4 crore from power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No; likely FX-related or export incentives. Management has not sold power; solar lapsed units were lost under the MSEDCL policy change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the ₹600-700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Renamed the executable order book; ₹500 crore set for FY27 given hurdles, with ₹600 crore possible next year on higher capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next capex and fundraising happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three good quarters needed first; land by December or March; project start by Q3 next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vestas concentration stay the same at ~₹600 crore revenue in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Vestas wants more allocation but capacity is going to new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) each allocating ₹100-150 crore; wind is ~₹400 crore of revenue, non-wind and gearboxes ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is offshore wind or Adani 5 MW participation viable?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani 5 MW parts often exceed 30 MT, so imported from China; Adani 5.2 MW bearing (6-7 ton casting) supplied. Offshore volumes not expected for 5-10 years; company focuses on 3-4 MW onshore.

541929|2026-09.headline: Synergy Green H1 FY27 PBDIT margin fell to 8.9% from 15.6% on input-cost inflation, while management reaffirmed 33% FY27 revenue growth and ~100 bp margin expansion.
541929|2026-09.overview: Management said H1 FY27 production rose 25.8% YoY and revenue rose 20.2%, but PBDIT margin compressed to 8.9% (Q2 at 10.2% vs 15.7% a year earlier) due to commodity and consumable inflation, logistics costs and under-absorbed ramp-up costs. Export shipments were delayed by ship and logistics constraints, building inventory that is carried at cost and not in revenue. Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 33% (about Rs 500 crore), exports up over 50% to about 30% of revenue, and FY27 margin up about 100 bp, implying 17-18% H2 EBITDA margin. Demand was described as strong, mainly from US wind OEMs, with greenfield expansion deferred until current capacity is stabilised.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 159.76 crore in H1 FY26 (as stated on call)

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 1.3 crore to Rs 3 crore (management cited both figures)

segments.name: Wind castings (domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Wind castings are about 70% of the portfolio; wind domestic revenue grew strongly in H1 YoY. OEM exports were in line with last year, with growth expected in H2.

segments.name: Gearbox castings
segments.commentary: Gearbox castings for wind are about 15% of the portfolio, with Flender and ZF among customers.

segments.name: Non-wind (cone crushers, coal pulverisers, mining, pumps)
segments.commentary: Remaining portion of the portfolio. Management is de-prioritising non-wind to focus capacity on wind, citing complexity and margin focus; machine-tool demand (e.g. Mahindra) could not be served.

segments.name: Machine shop
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 45-50% of machining capacity (20,000 tpa in-house); seven or eight products developed; management expects a good contribution in about 5-6 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 33% reaffirmed; management says the top line is not a constraint and Rs 500 crore turnover is achievable.
Exports expected to grow over 50% in FY27 and contribute about 30% of revenue (about 25% last year).
FY27 PBDIT/EBITDA margin expected to rise about 100 bp YoY; implies about 17-18% EBITDA margin in H2 versus 8.9% in H1.
Management guides EBITDA growth of about 50% and cash profit growth above 50% for FY27, with most of it in H2; net profit targeted to turn positive by year-end (described as roughly break-even).
Capacity utilisation expected at about 75% in H1, about 85% in H2, and about 80% for FY27 on 45,000 tpa.
Revenue potential from current 45,000 tpa capacity revised to Rs 600-650 crore (previously Rs 550-600 crore), citing inflation pass-through.
Management expects FY28 growth of about 25-30% and aims for about 25% CAGR; greenfield expansion is planned for FY29 and further debottlenecking of about 10-15% capacity is being explored.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa foundry (raised from 30,000 tpa in March 2026), plus about 20,000 tpa in-house machining and surface treatment; 10 MW captive solar.
Utilisation about 75% in H1 FY27, targeted at about 85% in H2 and about 80% for FY27.
Greenfield project needs about 15-18 months to build; to be phased, with stabilisation of current capacity first (about two quarters). Suzlon has approached the company to localise components.
Management said a further 10-15% capacity addition on the existing 45,000 tpa is being evaluated; no greenfield capex amount was given.
Captive solar and wind open-access power covers about 60% of electricity needs; captive solar yields about Rs 7-8/unit savings versus grid.
demand_pricing: Management reports no demand slowdown; US wind OEMs (Vestas, Nordex, and newer entrants) describe orders as open-book, with customers asking for more capacity. Demand is said to exceed 60,000 tpa against 45,000 tpa capacity.

Pricing: annual contracts are fixed for 12 months, with quarterly indexation on pig iron, CRC and furan. Pass-through is about 8-10% of cost increase, with a one-quarter lag; Q3 weighted average price increase about 5%. Management notes 100-150 bp margin impact in high-inflation periods.
Cost pressures: furan resin up 50%+ in Q1; commodities rising in Q2; logistics costs roughly threefold; Maharashtra power tariff up over 20% from April.
Export logistics: ODC shipments are constrained by ship availability; customers pay about 50-60% of component cost in freight for US shipments; October shipments reportedly 60-70% moving.

Competition: management is not concerned about a competitor's planned capacity addition (said to be about 3x), arguing Indian demand exceeds supply and OEMs will not single-source. Chinese castings face US tariffs, favouring Indian suppliers; RMB appreciation is expected to narrow the cost gap.

Customer base: works with 6 of the top 15 global wind OEMs (Vestas, Envision, Siemens Gamesa, Nordex, Adani, among others) and Flender and ZF in gearboxes. Nordex export order book above Rs 200 crore confirmed for the next 12 months; Envision still being onboarded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 33% FY27 growth shape up in H2, and is the 18% EBITDA guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 capacity is sufficient, with 150 crore+ per quarter run-rate and over 300 crore in H2. It expects 17-18% EBITDA margin in H2 and about 100 bp expansion for FY27, with the H1 margin at about 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Are elevated production costs expected to normalise, and what is the status of the long-term customer deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are pass-through with a one-quarter lag, and annual contracts are reset annually. A Nordex export deal of over Rs 200 crore is confirmed, with the US order book fully booked for 12 months; Vestas demand is described as very strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising capacity from competitors and the non-wind push pressure the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not concerned about competitors adding capacity, given demand above supply. Non-wind is being scaled back to concentrate on wind, and machine-tool demand is being declined for now.

qa_highlights.question: How long until the company is net profit positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors should focus on EBITDA and cash profit, which should grow over 50% in FY27. It aims to close the year in the green, with trailing four-quarter profit expected to be positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value revenue growth (about 20-23%) lagging volume growth (about 25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is inventory build-up from export shipment delays, which is held at cost and not recognised as revenue. Production growth of 25.8% is not the same as sales volume.

qa_highlights.question: What one-offs were in H1 electricity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: A High Court ruling on solar banking went in MSEDCL's favour, and retrospective charges were levied over two years. Management said about Rs 1.3-1.5 crore of retrospective cost is one-off, and tariff increases are permanent; wind open access is being used to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why not expand capacity aggressively given strong demand and the cyclical upturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution, skilled people and financing at fair valuations are the constraints, not demand. It wants to build demand before capacity and avoid overleveraging. Its target is 25% CAGR, and greenfield is planned for FY29.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (furan, pig iron, CRC) and logistics costs may hold H2 margins below the 17-18% EBITDA target.
Export shipment constraints could keep inventory elevated and push revenue below the 500 crore run-rate, especially with 50% export growth dependent on US shipping.
Only 100-150 bp of inflation pass-through is typical; the one-quarter pricing lag could compress margins if costs rise faster.
Execution risk: the 45,000 tpa plant has ramped only recently (from 30,000 tpa), and machine-shop utilisation is 45-50%.
Greenfield timing (15-18 months build, FY29 target) and funding plans remain unclear; management prefers raising capital at better valuations.
Net profit remains negative in the last two quarters; depreciation and interest weigh on PAT.
Power tariff hikes (Maharashtra over 20%) are a structural cost headwind.

Management was evasive on the greenfield timing and capex quantum, and on the exact H2 margin path.
key_quotes: So, as of now, I'm not seeing any, slowdown in, momentum.
So, you should look at a EBITDA value. than a profitability value.
Synergy always built market first, then added the capacity. It's not the other way around.

541956|2026-03.headline: IRCON FY26 revenue fell to Rs 9,502 crore (from Rs 11,131 crore) and PAT to Rs 592 crore; FY27 revenue guided flat at ~Rs 9,000 crore.
541956|2026-03.overview: FY26 total revenue was Rs 9,502 crore against Rs 11,131 crore in FY25, and PAT declined to Rs 592 crore from Rs 724 crore. Management said the order book rose to about Rs 24,984 crore (about 2x annual revenue), but sectoral headwinds and tougher bidding competition are pressuring margins. Management said FY26 revenue was about Rs 9,000 crore against earlier guidance of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, citing execution delays beyond its control, and guided FY27 at similar levels. Standalone core EBITDA margin is guided to 4.0-4.2% on the Q&A call (4.0-4.5% in a later answer), with consolidated PAT margin of 6.1-6.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue guidance drop from Rs 10,000-11,000 crore to about Rs 9,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to order book conversion difficulties in a tough market and to delays in land and clearances on existing projects. FY26 revenue was about Rs 9,000 crore, and FY27 is guided similar.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia/Gulf crisis put the Rs 9,000 crore revenue at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most FY27 revenue comes from the existing order book and that the impact is not expected immediately. It said the guidance would be reviewed if the crisis is prolonged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of international orders, given no large wins recently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is bidding in Africa but said the Gulf war and energy-price shock are weighing on sentiment. Current overseas projects are in Algeria, Myanmar, Bangladesh (completed), Nepal and Sri Lanka.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated non-current financial liabilities rise to about Rs 6,300 crore from Rs 4,750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other financial liabilities rose from Rs 584 crore to Rs 821 crore. It did not clearly explain the total increase on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated debt of about Rs 5,700 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the debt is project financing for 15-16 PPP SPVs (roads and highways, plus some coal connectivity rail), repaid over concession periods and not held at standalone level.

Phase 3 is funded wholly from internal cash, with a net debt-free balance sheet targeted by FY30.

541967|2026-09.headline: Sky Gold Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 61% YoY to INR2,391 crore, with reported PAT of INR129 crore up 93% and H1 operating cash flow positive at INR136 crore.

541974|2026-03.headline: Manorama FY26 standalone revenue rose 76.1% to INR 1,357 crore with EBITDA margin of 27.1% and PAT of INR 233.2 crore.
541974|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue grew 76.1% YoY to about INR 1,357 crore, with EBITDA of INR 367.7 crore (27.1% margin) and PAT of INR 233.2 crore (17.2% margin). Management announced a roughly INR 460 crore capex plan over two to three years covering solvent fractionation, a cocoa butter alternatives plant, refining and Burkina Faso raw material processing. Consolidated margins were softer as nine new subsidiaries were in their first year, and the company filed revised results due to a wrong file being uploaded.

541974|2026-09.headline: Manorama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.9% YoY to Rs 459 crore and PAT rose 51.8% to Rs 81 crore, with inventory building to Rs 1,000 crore.
541974|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 459 crore (up 41.9% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 118 crore (up 34.4%, margin 25.8%) and PAT of Rs 81 crore (up 51.8%, margin 17.6%). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 863 crore (up 40.8%), EBITDA Rs 224 crore (up 38%) and PAT Rs 159 crore (up 59.2%). Management attributed roughly 85% of growth to volume and 10-15% to price/mix. Inventory rose to Rs 1,000 crore at 30 September 2026 from Rs 728 crore in March, mainly from early procurement of shea and seasonal stock; management expects normalisation in H2. Leadership was restructured, with Deep Saraf moving to MD focused on operations and capacity, and Ashish Saraf moving to business development and strategy.

segments.commentary: Management said CBE and Shea stearin contribute about 70-75% of revenue, up from about 65-70% earlier, with a comfortable range of 70-80% at current capacity. Volume comes mostly from fractionation.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Value-added share of product mix is about 75%, up from 30-35% earlier, with a 70-80% target. Management cited the upgraded fractionation facility and mix as drivers of Q2 growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects healthy top-line growth for full FY27 and good growth in the coming quarter, but declined to quantify it or to give numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance.
Operating margin band of about 25-27% was described as reasonable, with modest quarter-to-quarter movements possible.
Debottlenecking of existing capacity is expected to be completed by end of FY27, targeting about 85% utilisation on the existing capacity (about 47,500 tonnes).
New capacity (Burkina Faso backward integration, fractionation and LATAM-related expansion) targeted for commissioning around Q3-Q4 FY28, with gradual contribution from FY29.
New capacity to start at 40-50% utilisation and reach 85-90% over 2-3 years.
Asset turnover guided at about 5-7x of investment at optimal utilisation.
Inventory expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and to be funded from the existing banking limit and internal accruals.

Existing capacity is about 47,500 tonnes at roughly 85% utilisation; a further 45,000 tonnes per annum of debottlenecking is planned.
Burkina Faso backward integration: land acquired, project in design and engineering in-house; detailed update promised in coming quarters.
Fractionation separation plan is in planning and engineering stage; no timeline given.
Management said the greenfield plan and debottlenecking are on track for FY28 Q3-Q4 commissioning, but the timeline was not changed.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no demand slowdown; products are supply-constrained and capacity is fully booked.
About 10-15% of Q2 revenue growth came from price/mix; about 85% from volume. Management said raw-material prices for shea do not track cocoa prices directly.
Freight and logistics costs rose sharply due to shipping and fuel price pressures, which hit gross margin in Q2.
Growth is a mix of new customers and existing customers; new customers are being added in new geographies.
Receivables rose from March 2026 levels, with management attributing this to the last 15 days of September revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is in gross profit, from higher freight costs linked to global macro events and fuel prices. No reclassification was mentioned.

qa_highlights.answer: About 85% from volume and 10-15% from price realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Burkina Faso backward integration and LATAM facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Burkina Faso design is in progress with land acquired. LATAM volumes are gradually ramping from existing capacity, which is fully booked; the LATAM facility timeline is FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex has been spent and when will it be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 70-75 crore has been invested. Commissioning is targeted for Q3-Q4 FY28, with contribution from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will CBE and shea stearin contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about 70-75%, with a comfortable range of 70-80% at current capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation of new fractionation capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity starts at 40-50% utilisation and reaches 85-90% in 2-3 years. Existing capacity is about 85%.

Pricing and realisation trend in renewed contracts; management said there is no direct link to cocoa prices but gave no numbers.

541988|2026-03.headline: AAVAS Q4FY26: net profit up 18% YoY to Rs 1.82 bn, NIM up 44 bps QoQ to 8.45%, GNPA 1.05%; management targets 20%+ AUM growth aspiration.

FY26 AUM reached Rs 234.5 bn (up 15% YoY) while FY26 disbursements grew 11% to Rs 67.8 bn, below the aspiration. Asset quality improved sequentially, with 1+ DPD at 3.17% (down 63 bps QoQ) and GNPA at 1.05% (down 14 bps QoQ). Management acknowledged weak volume productivity and opex growth outpacing AUM, and is pushing risk-adjusted pricing and direct sourcing to address these.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Vintage states show 1+ DPD and GNPA well below 4% and 1.25% of AUM; emerging markets are at 1+ DPD within 4% and GNPA within 1% of AUM. Q4 branch additions were concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, with focus also on Maharashtra and southern states.

Management expects the branch and people investments to start producing results in the next full year.

Management is shifting toward risk-adjusted pricing at branch level; it says early results are visible but the journey is gradual.
Average ticket size is to move only with inflation; no deliberate ticket-size expansion.

Sourcing mix: management is rebuilding direct sourcing (branch-driven, CSC, website, app with referral programme) while stating indirect channels will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the sector's medium-term growth stand and what are FY27/FY28 growth targets, and where does ROE settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is 20%+ AUM growth. Near-term focus is sharper execution across product, channel mix, geography and funnel leakages. High-teens ROE is the long-term target.

qa_highlights.question: With the PLR cut, how will spreads and disbursement yields evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a full-year cost of borrowing reduction of 62 bps stabilising, spread at 5.2%, and confidence in maintaining spreads at 5%+ via better product placement. It did not give a quantified yield outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been below 20% for two years and what is the channel plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed past performance to different variables and times. It plans to rebuild direct sourcing muscle while keeping indirect channels, and to invest in southern and other high-potential states.

qa_highlights.question: Has risk-adjusted pricing started and does higher yield imply higher risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing improvement began in FY26 across 435 branches and is progressing gradually. Management said higher yield does not mean higher risk and that it will not enter riskier segments or breach credit cost guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is competition from larger HFCs entering the company's ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 competition was a seasonal year-end push. It does not see a structural competitive impact on yields over the full year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opex-to-AUM trajectory and what are the tech-led efficiency use cases?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex rose in FY26 for branch and ESOP reasons. Management targets below 3% over 2-3 years and expects the branch investment to pay off in FY27. Tech spend is limited to small collection-software and AI investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why have loan volumes been flat or down despite headcount and branch growth, and what changed in April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called this an immediate priority, reported improved April numbers, and said productivity per person and revenue per field employee will be tracked quarterly. It also noted a shift to requiring realised instrument receipt in customer accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did repayment rates rise while balance transfer-outs fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer-outs were 5.5% for FY26 against a sub-6% cap. The rise in repayments was mainly from customer prepayments and part-payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East war and inflation shock?
qa_highlights.answer: No adverse trend in bounces or collections so far. The company is not financing energy-linked or directly affected profiles and is tracking 5-6 profiles it considers at risk.

risks_watch: Volume productivity: FY26 disbursement count was flat and home loan volumes were down YoY per analyst analysis, despite a larger headcount and branch base.

Competitive intensity from larger HFCs in affordable housing, particularly in quarter-end pushes.

541988|2026-06.headline: AAVAS Q1FY27: net profit up 23% YoY to Rs 1.71 bn, NII up 18%, but management sees spread falling below 5% over the year.
541988|2026-06.overview: Disbursements rose 41% YoY to Rs 16.1 bn on a low base, and AUM grew 15.4% YoY to Rs 239.3 bn as of June end. NIM rose 22 bps YoY to 7.70% and cost-to-income improved 254 bps to 43.7%. Asset quality metrics improved YoY, with 1+DPD at 3.76% and gross Stage 3 at 1.11%. Management flagged spread pressure from competition and a 10 bps PLR cut in June, taking the cumulative cut to 25 bps since March 2026, and an intent to regain home loan share.

segments.name: Home loans (HL)
segments.commentary: HL disbursement volumes grew 17% YoY in Q1 per management, and the company is refocusing on HL to rebalance the HL/NHL book toward roughly 65:35. HL carries 150-200 bps lower yield than NHL.

segments.name: Non-housing loans (NHL: LAP, MSME)
segments.commentary: Management described NHL as LAP and MSME products. The company said it has no builder loan product.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 22-23% top-line growth and 17-18% AUM growth; medium-term AUM growth of about 20%.
Management expects spread to fall to just below 5% over the rest of the year, while still expecting ROA and ROE to hold at planned levels.
Target to lift productivity per field resource from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh, to be achieved in about two years.
June disbursements exceeded Rs 600 crore; management aims to keep disbursements on a high run-rate through the next nine months.
Management reiterated credit-quality guidance and said it is confident of holding it.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 440 branches across 15 states during Q1; further branch expansion planned, with focus on faster branch break-even.
Borrowing liquidity: cash, cash equivalents and unavailed CC limits of Rs 18.8 bn; documented unavailed sanctions of Rs 4.85 bn as of June 30, 2026.
demand_pricing: Healthy competition across geographies with spread pressure; management said it is consciously pursuing HL share regain, which will cost some NIM.
Monthly AUM additions rose nearly 50% YoY; management said the company now reaches in three months what took about five months previously.
PLR cut 10 bps effective June 2026 (cumulative 25 bps since March 2026), with the company saying disbursement yield and portfolio yield are now close to each other.
Repayment rates rose to above 19% in the last two quarters versus a historical 16-17%; the uptick was in April and early May, especially in small-ticket loans above 14% interest, and eased in June.

Borrowings: 42% linked to external benchmarks (Repo, T-Bill, MIBOR) and 34% to sub-3-month MCLR, so about 76% reprices quickly; average borrowing tenor is longer than asset tenor, giving positive ALM.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition by product and geography, and can operating leverage offset spread compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees healthy competition and spread pressure, and expects spread to go below 5% for the full year. It says cost-to-income and revenue-per-resource levers should keep ROE and ROA near plan, even with some compression.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the June disbursement run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose in April and early May in small-ticket segments above 14%, then came back to trend in June. June disbursements were above Rs 600 crore, and the company is targeting 22-23% disbursement growth and 17-18% AUM growth over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the disbursement per branch that underpins the medium-term 20% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that current-year guidance is 17-18% AUM growth, with 20% as the medium-term target. Productivity is to rise from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh per field resource, which management said it would shorten to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company regain home loan market share, given a low two-year CAGR in HL files?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to rebalance HL and NHL toward about 65:35, with branch-level targeted acquisition for the next 9-12 months. HL volumes were up 17% YoY in Q1. It accepts a small NIM compression from the HL push.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gap between disbursement yield and portfolio yield after the June PLR cut, and what is the spread outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two yields are now nearly equal and the reported yield and spread already reflect the June cut. It expects spread to fall a little below 5% for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the recent RBI asset classification circular on repossessed assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the circular is under evaluation and any required change will be made.

Asset quality improved YoY, with 1+ DPD at 3.81% and Net Stage 3 at 0.70%. Management said AUM is on track to cross ₹250 bn in October 2026, and reiterated a 5%+ spread commitment despite a 25 bps repo hike earlier in October, with cost of borrowing expected to rise. The call was heavily focused on RO productivity, spread defence, LAP/HL mix shift, and insurance fee dependence.

segments.name: Home loans (HL) vs non-HL
segments.commentary: Target steady-state AUM mix is 65:35 HL to non-HL. Top-up loans to existing customers (about 5% of disbursements) are tagged as LAP, and booking above 60% construction stage is classed as LAP, which lifted LAP to about 21% of H1 disbursements versus about 14% of AUM.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME disbursement growth slowed to about 18% YoY in Q2 from about 32% previously. Management said this reflects risk and pricing discipline, not caution.

segments.name: Insurance fee income
segments.commentary: Insurance income is about 4% of PBT. Management aims to close about 50% of the regulatory revenue gap from 1 April 2027 by raising attachment rates.

guidance_outlook: Crossing ₹250 bn AUM in October 2026, with a long-term ambition of ₹500 bn AUM.
Management guided to AUM growth of 16-17% for FY27, and to disbursement growth of 20%+.
Spreads to stay above 5% on placements and at book level, even after the 25 bps repo hike, with cost of borrowing expected to rise and NIM and spreads expected to improve over coming quarters.
Productivity target of about 1.5 files per RO per month by end-FY27, scaling to 2 files; cost-to-income to fall below 40% medium term; opex-to-assets to fall below 3% (currently 3.33% in H1FY27).
Credit cost guidance within 25 bps; H1FY27 credit cost was 24 bps. Repayment rate expected at about 17%.
Medium-term volume growth build-up: about 20%+ CAGR, of which about 8% from branches, 10% from productivity and 5-7% from ATS.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 443 across 15 states at end-Q2; further branch expansion planned, with focus on faster branch breakeven.
21,500+ new customers added in H1FY27.
Long-term incentive plan rolled out mid-Q2; ESOP running for about 200 employees.
Headcount down about 150; management said this reflects repurposing and right-sizing, not job cuts.
demand_pricing: RO productivity: 1.1 files/month in Q1FY27, 1.2 in Q2FY27, 1.3 in September 2026. Revenue per RO up 29% in H1.
Home loan incremental yields have moved up about 8-10 bps; management said home loans are highly competitive.
PLR unchanged after the 25 bps repo hike; ALCO reviews PLR monthly.
Management said larger HFCs target a different ATS segment, so it sees no direct competitive pressure.
Borrowing mix: about 30% linked to repo; ₹16.79 bn raised in Q2FY27 at 7.66%.
Liquidity: ₹19.6 bn cash and un-availed CC limits, plus ₹3 bn documented un-availed sanctions.

qa_highlights.question: How has mortgage performance been in past weak monsoon or drought periods, and how does this affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mortgages have stayed resilient, lead indicators are improving month on month, and agri-income exposure is very limited. Exposure to Marathwada districts such as Latur is minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Will spreads be defended and will the 5% spread hold as repo-linked borrowings reprice in Q3 without a PLR hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated spreads above 5%, said incremental spreads are almost the same as the book spread today, and said PLR will be raised if ALCO sees the need.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to ₹500 bn AUM, and what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management broke the volume growth build-up into about 8% from branches, 10% from productivity and 5-7% from ATS, consistent with about 20%+ volume CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in LAP share, and what is the target HL/NHL mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-ups to existing customers are booked as LAP, and construction-stage clarification moved bookings above 60% completion into LAP. Steady-state AUM target is 65:35 HL to NHL.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the MSME disbursement growth slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of matching placements to risk and pricing, and that a quarterly change in mix should not be over-read.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance-fee risk from upcoming regulation, and how far can opex fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to recover about 50% of the expected regulatory loss by raising attachment rates, and to move cost-to-income below 40% in the medium term. Insurance is about 4% of PBT.

risks_watch: Cost of borrowing rising after the 25 bps repo hike, with about 30% of borrowings repo-linked; the spread defence depends on pricing pass-through and no PLR change so far.
Regulatory change to insurance distribution from 1 April 2027 could reduce fee income; management is targeting roughly half the expected loss to be recovered.
Productivity at 1.3 files per RO per month still short of the 1.5 target; scaling to 2 files depends on top-of-funnel growth.
Monsoon deficits in some states, with Maharashtra at about 19% of exposure; management says impact is minimal, but this needs monitoring.
Slower MSME disbursement growth (about 18% vs 32% earlier) and the HL/LAP reclassification could affect yield mix.
Headcount reduction of about 150 and a revamped incentive structure could affect frontline attrition.
