542011|2026-03.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.
542011|2026-03.overview: Management reported best-ever Q4 and FY26 results, with Q4 revenue of INR 2,119 crore (+29% YoY) and PAT of INR 303 crore (from INR 244 crore). Eight warships were delivered in FY26, including three on a single day, and the company said revenue from the bridges vertical crossed INR 200 crore for the first time. The order book fell to INR 15,324 crore, the first time it has dropped below INR 20,000 crore in five years, which management attributed to faster execution. The NGC corvette contract (~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE as L1) is still unsigned; management now expects signing in the June quarter, and it pushes NGC revenue recognition to H2 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.3% in FY25 (as cited by analyst; includes Q4 provision write-back benefit per analyst)
lower; first time below INR 20,000 crore in five years

segments.name: Warship / defence shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Warship order book about INR 11,361 crore. P-17 Alpha has about INR 5,868 crore remaining, NGOPV INR 5,168 crore and ASW Shallow Water Craft INR 2,035 crore. Eight warships delivered in FY26.

segments.name: Non-defence / commercial vessels
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 3,369 crore across Ocean Research Vessel (INR 749 crore), Coastal Research Vessels (INR 260 crore), Acoustic Research Ship (INR 456 crore), hybrid ferries (INR 207 crore), Multipurpose Vessels (INR 1,345 crore) and dredger (INR 66 crore).

segments.name: Naval guns and portable steel bridges
segments.commentary: Seven naval surface guns delivered in FY26, four completed Sea Acceptance Trials. 110 portable steel bridges delivered, including 30 for export; bridges revenue above INR 200 crore for the first time, export revenue above INR 270 crore.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract (~INR 33,000 crore) expected to be signed in the June 2026 quarter; no revenue planned in FY27 or H1 FY28; revenue to start in H2 FY28, major chunk from FY29.

FY27 revenue accrual expected to be 'very healthy', in line with the last three to four years; FY28 to be padded by remaining projects, NGOPV, commercial vessels and new orders. Management declined to confirm FY28 revenue will not dip.
EBITDA margins expected to be similar in FY27, and management will try to maintain similar margins in FY28 and FY29.
Capacity to rise from 28 platforms to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 via modernisation; plans for two brownfield and two greenfield yards (West Bengal and Gujarat).

Pipeline of about INR 1,50,000 crore of AoN-accorded RFPs (excluding NGC), with P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore) RFP expected in the current quarter; MCV (~INR 32,000 crore) and LPD (~INR 35,000 crore) RFPs by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current shipbuilding capacity is 28 platforms; expected to rise to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 through in-premises modernisation.
Planned expansion: two brownfield shipbuilding facilities in West Bengal and two greenfield facilities (one in West Bengal, one in Gujarat).
ASW Shallow Water Craft: four delivered, two at ~80% construction with basin trials done (delivery by mid-calendar 2026), last two at ~60% (delivery in FY27).
P-17 Alpha last ship at ~74% physical progress, delivery targeted in calendar 2026. NGOPV first ship launch planned on 20 May 2026; project completion in FY29.

Ocean Research Vessel ~50% complete, launch planned in calendar 2026. Acoustic Research Ship ~20% complete. 13 hybrid ferries (6 x 200-PAX, 7 x 100-PAX) to finish by end FY27; first two 100-PAX launches planned in May 2026. German 12-ship MPV: keel laid on three ships. Bangladesh dredger launch planned in FY27.
demand_pricing: Next Generation Corvette (NGC): price negotiations complete, ~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE is L1; contract slipped from 31 March 2026 target, now expected in June quarter; management says no red flags. Electronics is 55-60% of equipment cost, with BEL as a major sister-PSU supplier.

Live tenders: Multipurpose Vessels (2 ships, ~INR 1,500 crore, bid submitted), OPV for Coast Guard (5 ships, ~INR 2,000 crore) and 22 Interceptor Boats (~INR 1,000 crore), bids due around end May or early June 2026.

Upcoming RFPs in ~3 months: 120 Fast Interceptor Craft (~INR 3,500 crore, split 80/40), 31 Follow-On Water Jet FACs (~INR 3,500 crore) and seven P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore, split 4/3). MCV (12 ships, ~INR 32,000 crore, 8/4) and LPD (4 ships, ~INR 35,000 crore, 2/2) RFPs expected by end FY27.

Commercial tenders from Ministry of Shipping: four Platform Support Vessels (INR 1,200-1,500 crore), four MR tankers, six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels. European ship owners are in dialogue, citing pricing and quality versus China and Korea.
Cost escalation: existing contracts are fixed price, and vendor orders were placed earlier, so management reports no material impact; new bids will factor in commodity risk.

qa_highlights.question: Statutory defence committee report shows contracts expected over two years for warships and survey vessels fell to ~INR 18,900 crore from ~INR 42,000 crore. What does this mean for government focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the INR 18,900 crore figure reflects annual fund outflow, not intent. He cited AoNs, RFPs and approved Navy and Coast Guard roadmaps as evidence of continued focus.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional platforms remain relevant for armament and endurance. GRSE has developed subsurface and surface autonomous vessels, supplied one to a DRDO organisation, and targets the XL AUV under Make projects in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had kept a conservative provisional figure because three ships were delivered on the last day. After formalising deliveries and revenue with the Navy, final revenue came to about INR 7,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Price negotiations are complete. Contract signing was expected by 31 March but is now expected in the June quarter, with no red flags. Smaller projects are mostly single-yard awards, with 120 FAC and P-17 Bravo split between two yards.

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: NGC revenue recognition starts in H2 FY28, with the major chunk from FY29. Margins are expected to be similar in FY27 and the company will try to maintain them in FY28-FY29. Management did not confirm no FY28 revenue dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY25 and FY26 margins inflated by provision write-backs, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst cited 8.3% EBITDA margin in FY25 and 11.6% in FY26. Management said the current year margins will be similar but would not give a specific percentage, saying it is only Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment and systems are ~65% of project cost; electronics is 55-60% of that and machinery and systems 40-45%. First downstream orders expected within three months of contract signing, majority within three to six months. BEL expected to be a key partner.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial export projects will be selected for good margins. Warship projects, at ~INR 675 crore per ASW ship, still carry the best money and margins. Hybrid large vessels are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing contracts are fixed price and vendor contracts are fixed price too, so no material impact was reported. Time delays on steel and industrial gas were marginal. New bids will factor in uncertainty.

risks_watch: NGC contract signing has already slipped from 31 March to June quarter; any further delay would push the revenue ramp and reduce FY28 visibility.
Order book of INR 15,324 crore is down sharply; FY28 revenue is not guaranteed without new order wins, and no revenue recognition from NGC is planned until H2 FY28.

Commodity and steel cost escalation on new bids and possible time delays; existing contracts are fixed price.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Shipbuilding order book ₹12,980 crore (~95% of total); P-17 Alpha ~₹4,519 crore, NGOPV ~₹3,075 crore, anti-submarine shallow water craft ~₹1,815 crore, Ocean Research Vessel ₹740 crore, Acoustic Research Ship ₹450 crore, Multipurpose Vessels plus Dredger ~₹1,355 crore.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Order book about ₹96 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book about ₹219 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹158 crore; management says 100% indigenous.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹58 crore; about 90% indigenous per management.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹82 crore; co-production with foreign OEM targeting 55-60% indigenization.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract expected to be signed in Q2 FY27; revenue recognition to start in FY28, with eighth ship completion around 2034-35.
Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.
Indigenisation: management says ~80-85% overall by value; weapons ~60%, survival ~70%, float (hull) 100% but ~10% of cost, propulsion engines not yet indigenous; large survey vessel >80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port revitalisation is about ₹200 crore over 18 months. Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the indigenisation level and where is GRSE still import-dependent?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall indigenisation is about 80-85% by value. Hull/float is 100% but about 10% of cost, weapons about 60%, survival about 70%, and diesel alternators 100%; propulsion engines are not yet indigenous. Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses and employee costs QoQ, and what is the pay commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Contract workforce cost is sinusoidal with delivery timing and will rise when a couple of ships deliver. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

Order book fell to ₹13,596 crore; conversion of the ~₹80,000 crore of live RFPs (120 fast interceptor craft, 31 water jet FACs, P-17 Bravo) and the ~₹70,000 crore expected RFPs (mine sounder vessels, LPDs) is key.

542216|2026-06.headline: Dalmia Bharat Q1 FY27 volumes rose 9% YoY while EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores; Jaypee acquisition closed at INR2,850 crore EV.

EBITDA per ton rose 3% QoQ to INR1,055, but absolute EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores on lower volumes and fuel/packing cost inflation. The Jaypee Cement acquisition (5.2 Mt cement, 3.3 Mt clinker, Central India) closed on 29 May 2026, with a INR182 crore exceptional charge for stamp duty and transaction costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Dharmender Tuteja said that under business combination accounting, stamp duty does not add to fair-valued assets and is charged off; it is capitalised for tax and depreciation purposes.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Weather365 premium offering is seeing strong response, but no new product launch date was specified; Konark brand is being phased out.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA around 2x after JP acquisition

rows.label: Incentives return to prior levels
rows.why: Incentives fell to INR 25 crore in Q2 (down about INR 20 crore QoQ) and management expects them to return to prior levels in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Central EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Target stated but not proven; Central dilution about INR 50/ton in Q2 rising to INR 100-125/ton in Q3, and no utilisation breakeven point was disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident that East weakness, under-absorption and Central dilution are temporary and that Sep-Oct price gains of about INR 15/bag will help H2, but it was evasive on the Q4 fuel outlook, regional utilisation and state-level share loss, which analysts pushed on.

542323|2026-03.headline: KPI Green FY26 total income rose 56% to INR2,742 crore and PAT 57% to INR509 crore; management guides 40-50% growth.

Q4 FY26 total income was INR810 crore, EBITDA INR305 crore and PAT INR155 crore. Installed capacity stood at over 1.62 GW with 4.64 GW under work-in-progress, and operating cash flow rose to INR424 crore from INR208 crore. Interest cost rose sharply (about 130% to INR182 crore) as IPP capacity was commissioned ahead of full revenue, and management defended the margin and ROE trajectory with FY27-28 as the inflection years.

segments.name: CPP / EPC

IPP capacity of about 1.7 GW targeted for commissioning in FY27 (DC basis), with the 250 MW and 370 MW projects due October 2026, the 150 MW wind project November 2027, and a 300 MW SJVN project awaiting PPA signature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply?

qa_highlights.question: Botswana funding and equity structure?

qa_highlights.question: Grid stabilization charges in Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still evaluating project feasibility. It is not a rooftop player, and grid stabilization charges are not present in Gujarat.

542323|2026-06.headline: KPI Green Q1 FY27 total income rose 16% YoY to INR710 crore and EBITDA 21% to INR262 crore, but PAT fell to INR95 crore from INR111 crore.
542323|2026-06.overview: Revenue and EBITDA grew, with EBITDA margin up to 37% from 35%, but PAT declined as depreciation and interest on newly commissioned IPP assets were booked upfront while revenue ramps. Management said billing delays on utility-scale EPC projects pushed revenue into the next quarter, and cited geopolitical cost pressure on steel, cables, logistics and cranes. Portfolio reached 6.94 GW (1.87 GW installed, 5.07 GW WIP). Management guided to 30-40% revenue growth (softened from the chairman's 40-50%) and a PAT margin below the earlier 16-18% for FY27. segments.commentary: Portfolio of 4.37 GW; CPP order book approximately INR5,000-plus crore. Management said EPC is about 83% of total revenue, and that margins were hit by higher costs for steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes.

segments.commentary: Management expects Sun Drops to cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in FY27 across IPP and CPP; Sun Drops IPO is mentioned as upcoming.

Management expects the full earning contribution of new IPP assets to build through the rest of FY27, with most projects targeted for energization by September and full stabilisation in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 PAT margin meet the 16-18% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 and Q4 would recover only part of the Q1-Q2 gap, so the FY27 PAT margin would be lower than 16-18%; full benefit is expected in FY27-28.

542323|2026-09.headline: KPI Green Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to Rs 741 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore on higher IPP depreciation and finance costs.
542323|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 total income of Rs 741 crore (up 16% YoY from Rs 641 crore) and EBITDA of Rs 283 crore (up 22% YoY from Rs 232 crore), with EBITDA margin at 38%. Profit after tax fell to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance cost from IPP asset commissioning. H1 FY27 totals were total income Rs 1,451 crore, EBITDA Rs 545 crore, PAT Rs 187 crore and cash profit Rs 355 crore. Management guided FY27 PAT of about Rs 500 crore, with a binding agreement to acquire 507.9 MW of operating Gujarat wind assets for an enterprise value of about Rs 240 crore.

segments.commentary: Commissioned 269 MW solar for Coal India's Khavda project and 128 MW solar for Mahagenco in Maharashtra. Secured an IPP order of about Rs 2,000 crore for a 500 MW solar project for NACoP Purja Pvt Ltd in Rajasthan.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock valued below peers, given the IPP business's recurring cash profits?

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider demerging the IPP business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a demerger needs enough scale first, and it would take time once the IPP base is built to around 2.1 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 profit expectation and will wind orders go to the EPC arm?

qa_highlights.question: How will funding for BESS manufacturing and IPP build-out be raised, and what is the Sun Drop listing timeline?

542399|2026-03.headline: Chalet Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR5,711 million and EBITDA 8% to INR2,786 million, while hospitality RevPAR fell 3% on Mumbai weakness.
542399|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was uneven: a soft January in Mumbai and a March slump from West Asia tensions cut foreign-tourist room nights (about 9,000 lost in March alone), with management putting the disruption at 10-12% of business. Hospitality revenue grew 3% to INR4,740 million and EBITDA 1% to INR2,248 million, with margin down 102 bps to 47.4%. Ex-residential revenue grew 6% to INR5,706 million with a 49.1% EBITDA margin. Management guided to a strong recovery in the second half and planned about INR30 billion of capex over FY27-FY29, mainly from internal accruals, while adding the Udaipur resort and a 330-key Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,740 million (+3%) and EBITDA INR2,248 million (+1%); Mumbai underperformed while South hotels and resorts (Westin Rishikesh) did well. Resort occupancy averaged about 43% for FY26, targeted to trend toward 60%.

segments.name: Commercial real estate
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,061 million (+55%) at an 83.1% EBITDA margin. March 2026 monthly rental run-rate INR280 million; committed occupancy about 88%, with Bangalore above 83% (management later cited about 91%) and Powai at 90%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Phase 1 has 152 units handed over and one pending. Phase 2 (168 units) is due for handover in FY27, plus 160,000 sq ft of commercial space yet to be developed.

guidance_outlook: Monthly CRE rentals expected to scale to about INR300 million during FY27; CIGNUS II commissioning in FY28 to drive a step change.
Planned capex of about INR30 billion over FY27-FY29 covering hospitality and CRE, including announced acquisitions, expected to be funded through internal accruals.
Enabling approval for debt raise of up to INR10 billion; management said there is no immediate plan to raise incremental debt.
Management expects a strong recovery and bounce-back in the second half of FY27 as marriages return from the Middle East to India.
Management expects Q1 FY27 to be fairly strong, with April stronger than expected, May strong against a weak base, and June steady.
Management expects leisure portfolio EBITDA margins to reach at least the mid-40s; city hotel margins expected to remain stable rather than expand.
Management expects RevPAR growth in the mid to high single digits to translate into mid-to-high double-digit room revenue growth for FY27 (answered 'Yes').
capex_capacity: Operating keys 3,389 with about 1,655 pipeline keys across 7 assets, taking total to over 5,000 keys.
Udaipur resort acquired for INR1,710 million (144 keys on 8.2 acres); upgrade to upper-upscale planned, with timelines, capex and brand not yet disclosed.

Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad: 330-key ultra-luxury hotel outside Mindspace Madhapur on a warm-shell lease from Mindspace REIT; pure construction capex INR5,600 million (INR560 crore) including 40,000 sq ft commercial space, fit-out largely after possession in Q4 FY28; launch by end FY29.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by end FY27, though West Asia has pressured labour availability.
Taj project at Delhi International Airport: 70 rooms to launch by Q4 FY27, balance inventory in phases.
Bangalore added 129 rooms (management also cited 121 rooms in Q&A); Athiva Khandala had its first full quarter at full inventory, with ADR north of INR15,000.
Capital WIP and assets not yielding returns at INR8.3 billion at year-end (management split: IPUC about INR486 crore, CWIP INR132 crore, inventory about INR269 crore).
demand_pricing: Mumbai ADR growth of 0-2% and occupancy down 0-2 pp in Jan-Mar 2026 per industry reports, versus India ADR growth of 6-8%; the Powai property was also hit by CIGNUS II construction.
February was very strong, with some South hotels up over 35% YoY; March cancellations cost about 9,000 foreign-tourist room nights, and management put total disruption at 10-12%.
Management said domestic traveller demand showed no meaningful decline; the group/MICE share rose from 20% to 22% of business in the last month.
Management reiterated that Athiva ADR is north of INR15,000 and expects Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad ADR around INR25,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a subsidiary-level minority dilution at DIAL rather than debt or internal funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a one-time project-level minority partnership, not a capital decision; the balance sheet is strong and no fundraising is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-FY29 capex funding mix and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Khanna said the entire INR30 billion for announced projects will be funded through internal accruals, with no major borrowing unless a strategic acquisition arises.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CRE leasing taking until FY28 to fully let out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the leasing comment applied to CIGNUS II; existing inventory is above 90% occupied, so only about 10% remains to lease there.

qa_highlights.answer: Capex is INR560 crore construction cost (INR630 crore earlier included IDC and lease deposit); management expects ADR around INR25,000 but declined to give stabilisation timing or lease terms.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the INR800 crore of capital WIP sit on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Khanna said about INR486 crore is in IPUC, INR132 crore in CWIP and about INR269 crore in inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: City hotel margins are at a stable point and will not expand much; leisure margins can rise to the mid-40s, CRE margins are at 83-84%, and Bangalore ramp-up will matter.

542399|2026-06.headline: Chalet Q1 FY27 core revenue up 10% to INR5,140mn and EBITDA up 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%.
542399|2026-06.overview: Excluding residential, revenue grew 10% YoY to INR5,140mn and EBITDA rose 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%; net profit was INR861mn. Hospitality RevPAR rose 6.5% on 8.5% ADR growth, with leisure resorts up 19% while FTA-dependent markets (Hyderabad, Bangalore) and MMR (Powai, Vashi) lagged. Commercial real estate revenue rose 18% to INR865mn with 85% margin, and the June 2026 rental run rate reached INR290mn per month. Management said August looks positive but declined to guide for the quarter given day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: Slightly up vs March 2026 after acquisitions

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,185mn (+9%) and EBITDA INR1,784mn (+11%), margin 42.6%. Leisure portfolio RevPAR +19%; Pune high double-digit RevPAR growth; Hyderabad and Bangalore weak on occupancy due to FTA decline.

segments.name: Commercial real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR865mn (+18%) and EBITDA INR735mn (+21%). Portfolio committed about 91%; LOI signed for 66,000 sq ft more at Bangalore; monthly rental guided to INR300-320mn during FY27.

segments.name: Residential (Koramangala)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 completed; INR73mn revenue and INR31mn EBITDA recognised this quarter. 168 Phase 2 units to be handed over during FY27. Prior-year comparison distorted by one-time recognition.

segments.name: MMR portfolio
segments.commentary: Powai and Vashi (over 60% of MMR inventory) lagged on construction and renovation; JW Sahar saw good ADR growth with steady occupancy. MMR is about 43% of hospitality revenue in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Planned capex of about INR30bn over FY27-FY29 across hospitality and commercial real estate, largely funded by internal accruals.
Monthly rentals expected to scale to INR300-320mn during FY27; CIGNUS II Powai commissioning to drive step-change from FY28.
Taj Delhi Airport: minimum 70 rooms to launch in Q4 FY27, balance in phases within Q1 of next fiscal.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by FY27 end.
South Goa hotel construction expected to start by end of the current quarter, after the rainy season.
Management declined to guide for the quarter; August described as overall positive, September too far out.

Added 129 keys at Bangalore; Dukes Retreat rebranded to Athiva with 67 additional keys.
Udaipur (Athiva) expansion awaiting approvals from local authorities and army cantonment; clarity expected in one to two quarters.
Mindspace projects at Hyderabad and Airoli have begun excavation; both on track.
CIGNUS II Powai adds 0.9mn sq ft of office space; INR10,914mn of net debt allocable to under-construction or yet-to-be-operational assets.
demand_pricing: Leisure resorts occupancy about 51% this quarter; management sees stabilised resort occupancy at 60-65%.
Athiva Khandala weekend rates sustained above INR15,000; weekday MICE demand still needs building.
Powai porch and Westin banquet connectivity due by quarter end; noisy construction to end in one to one and a half quarters.
FPS (Fairmont-adjacent MMR asset) renovation done at INR93 crore; rebranding to be announced in coming weeks.
Management said supply in MMR has been absorbed, with no major new supply expected in the next one to two years.
Commission rates paid to OTAs and GDS described as bottom-end of the market; OTA and transient mix fell but management said this is not a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for MMR underperformance, booking window, MICE, and competition including Fairmont near JW Marriott Sahar?
qa_highlights.answer: JW Sahar outperforming on ADR with steady occupancy; Powai under construction and FPS renovation driving near-term pain. Supply absorbed with no major supply in next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will leisure reach 20% of portfolio target change, and Inder Residency expansion potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy unchanged: leisure stays at about 20% of portfolio. Udaipur expansion awaiting two approvals; no firm number yet; existing building work proceeding.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for resort occupancy to reach 70%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Resorts stabilise at 60-65%; Q1 was 51% and expected to keep improving. Athiva Khandala creating a premium MICE market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8.5% ADR growth from pricing or channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: No major channel mix change; special corporate rates were raised slightly to retain them, and crew business increased.

qa_highlights.question: July trends and current outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter started strongly, but visibility has worsened as the West Asia situation changes every 5 to 10 days. August looks positive; no quarterly guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term MMR occupancy ceiling, can it return to 77%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes Powai and FPS can return to prior levels and go beyond. FPS was at about 140% fair share before refurbishment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: FTA arrivals stay flat; management said normalisation takes about 60 days after resolution, and sentiment has deteriorated again.
MMR: Powai and Vashi occupancy recovery depends on construction ending and the porch reopening in H2 FY27.
Bangalore relocation and group business softness; Hyderabad FTA exposure.
Leisure occupancy may be partly driven by domestic shift from outbound travel; management says the 60-65% target is a given but timing is uncertain.
Goa and Udaipur project timelines depend on local and army approvals.
Net debt rising with acquisitions; INR10.9bn tied to assets not yet operational.

542399|2026-09.headline: Chalet Q2 FY27 core revenue rose 11% YoY to INR 5,110 million and EBITDA 13% to INR 2,274 million, with margin up 110 bps to 45%.

Hospitality RevPAR rose 7.2% on 11.3% ADR growth, while resorts grew RevPAR 34% and MMR business hotels lagged due to Powai construction and weaker foreign travel. Management flagged that consolidated YoY comparisons are distorted by the Phase-I Koramangala residential handover in Q2 FY26, with Phase-II handovers (168 units, RERA date December 2026) to be booked in Q3 FY27. Credit rating was upgraded to IND AA by India Ratings, and planned capex for FY27-FY29 was raised to INR 34-36 billion after adding two ATHIVA properties; Taj Delhi airport timing may slip on GRAP restrictions.

542459|2026-03.headline: Kranti Industries crossed ₹100 crore consolidated revenue in FY26 (+28%), with standalone PAT of ₹260 lakh versus a ₹75 lakh loss in FY25.
542459|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described by management as transformational: consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore for the first time, and the company returned to profit. Standalone revenue rose 30% to ₹93.88 crore, with EBITDA up 63.7% to ₹1244 lakh and margin improving from 10.5% to 13.3%. Q4 standalone revenue of ₹29.31 crore was the highest quarterly figure on record, up 60.2% YoY and 28.2% QoQ, though Q4 EBITDA of ₹167 lakh reflects startup costs at the new Jaipur plant. The company also entered defence machining via AVNL orders and took over a Jaipur plant on lease from 1 January 2026.

segments.commentary: EV-related components contributed about 5.3% of FY26 revenue across Kalyani Techno Forge (one passenger-car EV part, one production line running for about 12-15 months), Dana group and Eka Mobility.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Entered defence via machining orders from AVNL in FY26. Management is targeting PSU customers directly rather than as a Tier-2/3 supplier; the company expects it to take 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position.

segments.name: Jaipur plant (Plant-4)
segments.commentary: Fourth facility, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity, with commercial operations from 1 January 2026. Utilisation was below 40% in its first quarter, and FY27 revenue guidance is ₹12-14 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit YoY revenue growth from here, subject to no extraordinary events.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 18-20% at about 85% utilisation with a richer product mix, targeted for FY28 rather than FY27.

Priorities for FY27: ramp Jaipur utilisation, expand exports, deepen presence in defence, industrial, construction equipment and EV, and improve working capital efficiency.

capex_capacity: Jaipur facility (Plant-4) commissioned; commercial production from 1 January 2026, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity.

qa_highlights.answer: It gives entry into the northern auto-ancillary belt, a ready plant with business, and a dedicated customer who will route 100% of its machining to Kranti under an exclusive agreement.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can defence scale and what is the approach?

542460|2026-09.headline: Anup Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue rose 46% QoQ to INR182 crores, but EBITDA margin was 9.6%; FY27 guidance is INR840-860 crores revenue.
542460|2026-09.overview: Q2 consolidated revenue was INR182 crores, up 46% from Q1, with EBITDA of INR17.5 crores (9.6%) as fixed-cost under-absorption (fixed cost INR62 crores) and about 6% elevated material cost plus about 2% inward freight weighed on margins. Management attributed weak H1 to low order booking in H1 FY26 (about INR250 crores versus a normal INR500-600 crores requirement), which left thin-margin orders executing in H1 FY27. FY27 guidance is revenue of INR840-860 crores and EBITDA of INR120-128 crores (14-15% margin), implying a 20-22% margin in Q4 on newer, better-priced orders. Order intake and the pending order book improved: pending order book is INR941 crores as of date, and new order intake for FY27 is INR674 crores as of date.

542484|2026-03.headline: Arvind Fashions Q4 FY26 revenue up 14.8% to INR1,365 crore NSV; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion.
542484|2026-03.overview: Q4 NSV rose 14.8% YoY to INR1,365 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income at INR189 crore (vs INR159 crore) and a 50 bps margin gain. Reported PAT was INR47 crore against a loss of INR93 crore a year earlier; comparable PAT grew 56%. For FY26, revenue grew 14%, EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 13.4%, comparable PAT grew 62% to INR124 crore, and ROCE crossed 23%. Direct channels reached 56% of sales, and management guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps margin expansion in FY27 despite macro and commodity risks.

segments.name: Online B2C
segments.commentary: Grew over 40% in Q4, raising share to 14% from 11%, as the company shifts away from B2B online. Management expects online B2C to sustain 20%+ growth over the years.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: USPA posted its highest-ever growth in Q4; PVH brands and Flying Machine each grew over 10% (Flying Machine retail LTL in double digits, B2C up 70%). Arrow was subdued due to a one-time model change and weak wedding calendar.

qa_highlights.question: Can 30-40 bps margin expansion hold with cotton prices rising and A&P spend increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India-based sourcing, cost-control measures, selective price increases and mitigation already in motion. It said it is cautious but optimistic on the guidance.

Off-highway and commercial vehicles grew 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ, and Products revenue grew 5% QoQ and 25% YoY. 542652|2026-03.headline: Polycab Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY with EBITDA margin at 13.1% and record quarterly PAT of INR 7.9 bn, while Cable & Wire volumes grew only low single digits.
542652|2026-03.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY, with domestic cables up 30% and combined volume growth in low single digits. EBIT margin was 13.1%, and Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+. Cables outpaced wires, and institutional sales grew faster than channel.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 47% YoY, the ninth straight quarter of outperformance versus industry. EBIT margin was 4.1%, and FY26 EBITDA margin was mid-single digit. Solar was the largest FMEG category, growing 2x; premium fans were about 25% and premium lighting about 35% of segment revenue.

segments.name: International (exports)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY and contributed 4.4% of consolidated revenue in Q4. Full-year export share was 5.4%, and Middle East was about 16% of FY26 exports, which was hit during the quarter.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 15% YoY to INR 5,098 mn on project execution timing. Segment profit was INR 386 mn, a 7.6% margin. Sustainable margin is guided at mid to high single digits.

guidance_outlook: Project Spring: Cables & Wires to grow at 1.5x industry growth; FMEG at 1.5x-2x industry growth.
Near to mid-term EBITDA margin guided at 12-14%; long-term 11-13%.
Exports to reach more than 10% of revenue by FY30; management expects exports to grow beyond 5% in FY27 and hopes to get there sooner.
Working capital cycle expected to revert to 45-50 days from 25 days in Q4.
Dividend payout to exceed 30% by FY30 (27.2% in FY26).
Capex of INR 60-80 bn over 5 years; FY27 capex guided at INR 12-16 bn per year; FY30 capex of INR 60-80 bn cited as Project Spring target.
EHV capacity expected on stream by end of calendar 2026, with revenue contribution from FY28.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is mid-70s (75-76%); management says plants practically reach early 90s but a sustainable level is 80-85%.
FY26 capex was about INR 14.8 bn, including roughly INR 15 bn invested in capacity expansion; the company plans INR 1.2-1.6 bn of capacity addition every year.
Around 90% of capex goes to Cable & Wire capacity (largely fungible), about 5% to backward integration and 3-4% to FMEG.
EHV (extra high voltage) capacity is on track to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; about 50% of domestic EHV consumption is imported.
Management says there will be no scenario where Polycab runs out of capacity over the next 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price hikes of about 18-19% were taken from January to March; pass-through of copper, aluminium and PVC is described as complete and in tandem with input costs.
Volume growth was low single digits in Q4 as West Asia tensions, pollution-related construction halts and PVC price spikes (60-80% in early March) hit primary and secondary sales.
FY26 Cable & Wire volume growth was 18%, versus industry growth of 11-12%, with domestic wires and cable organised market share at 30-31% (up 300-400 bps over FY25's 26-27%).
Channel is about 90% of business and institutional about 10%; channel margins are 3-4% higher than institutional. Institutional mix was 2-3 points higher in Q4.
Demand sectors: power 40-45% of cables, manufacturing and private industry 35-40%, mobility 10-12%, energy and exploration 5-6%.
Power capacity additions in FY26 were about 55-56 GW, nearly double FY25; management expects demand to defer by weeks, not be lost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined volume growth was low single digits, with cables ahead of wires. Cumulative price hikes were about 18-19% from January to March.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, Brent around USD 100/bbl and a record-low rupee (INR 94.83/USD) raise input and inflation risk; the company's stated pass-through has so far held.

Institutional mix rising reduces margins (channel is 3-4% higher); watch the mix next quarter.

FMEG margins (EBIT 4.1%) remain well below the 8-10% EBITDA target for FY30; watch the trajectory.
Export share fell to 4.4% in Q4; Middle East recovery timing and the US distribution ramp are open questions.
EHV commissioning by end of calendar 2026 and first revenue in FY28.

542652|2026-06.headline: Polycab Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 39% YoY, record PAT of INR 7,967 million (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8%.
542652|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 39% YoY with EBITDA up 32% and margin at 13.8%, about 70 bps sequentially higher. Record quarterly PAT of INR 7,967 million at a 9.7% margin. Wires & Cables grew 39% and FMEG grew 71%, while EPC revenue fell 11%. Volume growth in domestic cables and wires was low to mid-single digit against a high base of about 26% last year, and exports declined on the Middle East disruption. Management cut prices by 3-4% in early July and said channel destocking followed the sharp fall in copper and aluminium prices in June.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 71% YoY, the tenth straight quarter of outperforming industry growth. EBIT margin was 8%; premium mix reached about 25% of the portfolio (fans about 33%, lighting about 38%). Solar more than doubled and is now the largest category, though still below 50% of FMEG.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR 3,077 million, down 11% YoY on project timing; profitability was INR 338 million at an 11% margin. Management attributed the dip to milestone-linked revenue recognition.

guidance_outlook: Wires & Cables medium- to long-term EBIT margin guidance maintained at 11% to 13% under Project Spring.
FMEG targets EBITDA margins of 8% to 10% by FY30 (full-year basis) and growth at 1.5x to 2x industry growth.

T&D: about 2,000 circuit km added in April-May FY27; CEA estimate of about 17,000 ckm for FY27 versus about 20,000-21,000 ckm average for FY26-FY30.
demand_pricing: Domestic W&C volume growth was low to mid-single digit on a base of about 26% last year (cables above 25%, wires above 20%); wires grew high single digit and cables low to mid single digit.

Channel stocking was below expectation in June as aluminium fell about 18-20% and copper fell from about INR 14,000 to INR 13,100-13,200; healthy channel stocking is about 20-25 days.

Channel contributes about 90% of W&C sales; Polycab estimates it gained 3-4% market share over the last 10-12 months (per last update).
FMEG: fans, pipes and conduits, lighting and switchgear all grew faster than their industry categories; FMEG ex-solar volume and price split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What were the price hikes and volume growth YoY, and how will pricing look in Q2 given copper?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic cable and wire volume grew low to mid-single digit on a high base; no Q2 copper guidance given, as pricing is cost-plus. A 3-4% price revision was taken in early July.

qa_highlights.question: Acceptances rose; how much are LC/acceptances and is their interest booked in finance costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about 100-110 days, LC-based payables about 80-90 days, and receivables 20-30 days, producing a 15-day cycle this quarter. The accounting treatment was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre and optical fibre opportunity, and export trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres could add about INR 3.5 crores of cable per MW, an INR 20,000-25,000 crore market over 6-8 years, and Polycab already supplies conventional cables to some existing sites. Exports are recovering with a healthy order book; Middle East was 20-24% of Q1 exports.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Net fibre price risk and why EPC revenue fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre for the execution period is already secured, so Bharat Net is not exposed to higher fibre prices. EPC revenue timing is milestone-linked and may shift between quarters, with no material full-year dip expected.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume growth outlook and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 10-12 month trends rather than quarters; FY26 volume growth was 18% and 1.5x market growth is reiterated. Share gains of 3-4% were reported in the last update, with the next analysis expected after peers report.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of channel stocking benefiting Q1, and is the margin improvement limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking was below expectation as raw-material prices fell in June. Margins were supported by wires mix and channel mix, offset by weaker exports and operating leverage; the company targets the 11-13% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG margin trajectory, and is 8% EBIT sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were operating leverage on a low base, a premium mix of about 25% overall, and regional product strategies. Management expects seasonality and targets 8-10% EBITDA margin for FMEG for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the data-centre and T&D demand strong enough to move industry growth, given the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 1 GW of data-centre additions alone would be limited, but said T&D demand is accelerating, with about 15% cable content in T&D spend and transformer makers' order books at about 2.5x revenue.

542652|2026-09.headline: Polycab Q2 FY27 revenue rose 53% YoY with PAT of INR 9,900 million (+43%) and EBITDA margin of 14.4%, all record highs.
542652|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-yearly revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue up 53% YoY and all segments contributing to growth. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to a 14.4% margin, up more than 50 bps QoQ, helped by mix, operating leverage and copper price pass-through. Wires and Cables grew 47% and FMEG grew 124%, with FMEG crossing a 10% EBIT margin for the first time. Management said the Asier Metals IBC matter is under NCLAT review, with order reserved and no material impact expected.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue +124% YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of industry-leading growth, and seventh consecutive profitable quarter per CEO. EBIT margin 10.1%, first time above double digits. Solar (inverters only, traded) was the main driver; fans premium mix about 33% and lights about 38%.

Export order book strong in US, Europe, LATAM, Asia and Middle East; now selling to 94 countries.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, operating leverage, premium mix and bundled solution offerings for FMEG. Targets are FY30-based; long-term FMEG EBITDA margin of 8-10% is still cited, and a 10.1% EBIT margin is described as very high.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pricing response to new wires entrants like UltraTech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no action on pricing so far, that the entrant's wires presence is a small share of the business, and that the company gained 1-1.5% share annually (3-4 points last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be soft on a high base, and what is FY volume growth expected to be?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a seasonal copper-price related inventory build or delay in offtake?

542665|2026-03.headline: Neogen Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 247 crore with 17.8% EBITDA margin; FY27 standalone guidance INR 875-950 crore.
542665|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 247 crore, almost entirely volume-driven, with EBITDA up 21% to INR 44 crore and margin at 17.8% despite Dahej replacement and toll manufacturing costs. PAT was INR 11 crore for the quarter and INR 29 crore for FY26 on revenue of INR 862 crore. Battery materials (Neogen Ionics) remain the core growth push: Dahej Phase 1 is budgeted at INR 428 crore and Pakhajan Phase 2 revised to INR 1,367 crore, with commissioning now guided within FY27. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue guidance at INR 875-950 crore, excluding battery sales, and separately guided INR 300 crore-plus from battery chemicals, weighted to H2.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash from operations H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26
financial_highlights.value: INR 14.6 crore inflow vs INR 246.1 crore outflow

segments.name: Organic Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 194 crore, up 7% YoY. Bromine derivatives about 40-45% of revenue, advanced intermediates about 30%, organolithium and lithium the balance.

segments.name: Inorganic Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 53 crore, up 145% YoY, mostly volume-driven as customers bought ahead of expected lithium price rises.

segments.name: Neogen Ionics (battery materials)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 13 crore to Q4 FY26 revenue and INR 36 crore for FY26, of which electrolyte was below INR 10 crore and salt was the majority.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone (non-battery) revenue guided at INR 875-950 crore, including Dahej replacement plant output, against an original INR 950-1,000 crore target; management aims for the upper end and above if organolithium and lithium outperform.
Battery chemicals revenue guided at INR 300 crore-plus for FY27, mostly in H2 with sequential growth each quarter; excludes commodity price upside.

Electrolyte commercial manufacturing targeted for H1 FY27; electrolyte salt in H2 FY27. Dahej Phase 1 (1,000 tons balance plus 500 tons intermediate) targeted by Q3 FY27, with SCOD of February 2027 approved by lenders; Pakhajan Phase 2 SCOD March 2027.

FY28 tentative target of around INR 1,100 crore plus at full utilisation for the standalone business; FY28 battery revenue expected INR 1,200-1,400 crore by management estimate; FY29 consolidated revenue of INR 3,700-4,200 crore cited (standalone INR 1,200-1,250 crore plus battery INR 2,500-2,900 crore).
Targeted ROCE of 18-20% on the revised battery capex.
Commercial electrolyte supply from Dahej expected by July or August 2026 after completing audit corrections.
Morita equity contribution of USD 20 million expected in H1 FY27; management says funds from promoter (INR 161 crore) and JV plus insurance are sufficient to complete projects.
capex_capacity: Dahej Phase 1 budget INR 428 crore, completion targeted February 2027; Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion March 2027. Revision reflects Morita technology alignment, a 500 MT intermediate lithium salt addition and localisation of components.
Pakhajan electrolyte plant completed mechanical assembly and entered trial run; 30,000 tonne electrolyte plant under trial production, built on Mitsubishi technology per management.
Salt and additive capacity at Dahej: 5,500 tonnes total (about 4,000 tonnes salt and 750-1,500 tonnes additive), plus 500 tonnes intermediate over and above.

Remaining FY27 capex around INR 600-700 crore for Neogen Ionics plus about INR 100 crore for Neogen; no major capex planned for FY28 at present. Neogen Ionics gross block expected INR 1,700-1,800 crore at end-FY27; standalone gross block INR 450-550 crore.
Organolithium capacity raised 2.5x to 300 tonnes per year from about 120 tonnes; management expects 80-90% utilisation this year and a small capex possible next year.
demand_pricing: Lithium carbonate around USD 24-25/kg versus management's long-term stable band of USD 15-25 (centre about USD 20); management does not factor commodity upside into guidance because it is passed through.
Bromine prices elevated but stable after shipments from Dead Sea Bromine; contracts limited the Q4 impact. Management budgets bromine at about INR 300 plus or minus 50.

Chinese LiPF6 salt pricing was 30-50% below Neogen's formula price at start of the year; the gap is now about 20-25%. Electrolyte pricing guided at USD 6-8/kg (current lithium price about USD 7-9/kg), with USD 7-7.5 as average.

Two electrolyte customers have qualified Neogen; two more are validating Neogen electrolyte against Chinese electrolyte; two more start in 2027. Management says US electrolyte makers' site audits are complete with commercial clearances pending.

CRM complex output rose to about 718,000 MT with utilisation at 70.9% annualised, and pipes and tubes output rose to 201,000 MT from about 177,000 MT. The focus has shifted to the Bokaro greenfield downstream steel complex, with cold trials guided before end-May 2026 and hot trials in June; meaningful Bokaro sales are expected from Q2 FY27.

542669|2026-09.headline: BMW Industries Q2 FY27 operating income rose 25.3% YoY to Rs 182 crore; PAT up 42.7% to Rs 22 crore, with Bokaro colour-coating line now in operation.

rows.label: Colour-coated pricing pressure from new capacity
rows.why: Management expects price pressure from new colour-coated capacity and peers Shyam Metalics and Godawari are expanding; margins expected stable on rupee-per-ton basis, while Galvalume/ZAM hedging is not yet in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term market story and Bokaro build (COD Sept 2027, colour-coating line live), but cautious on near-term specifics, declining FY27 revenue guidance and order-book details; analysts pushed on the one-off other income, zinc/aluminium hedging and working capital.
